name: Content-first responsive composition
summary: Choose columns, region prominence and stacking/reduction by user task and available width instead of preserving desktop geometry unchanged.
problem: Fixed multi-column page geometry may obscure essential content or introduce unnecessary horizontal scrolling on constrained viewports.
context: Multi-region interfaces with main content, secondary panes/navigation and a narrow-screen mode.
observed_solution: Begin from content priorities; use an intentional responsive grid/region strategy (reflow, grouping, pane placement, optional collapse) while preserving essential access and meaningful order.
rationale: WAI discusses viewport adaptation (O10); GOV.UK starts small-screen layouts in one column (O11); Carbon differentiates layout models by task (O18,O20); Primer advises simplifying multi-column screens (O22); pinned PageLayout implements width and pane-region variants (O26–O28).
tradeoffs: High-density and side-by-side comparison tasks may need controlled horizontal navigation.
Collapsing critical controls without alternative access can destroy functionality; semantics and reading order still require testing.
applicability: Applications whose sidebar, navigation or secondary pane can move or collapse on smaller viewports without losing task access.
non_applicability: Data views where 2D layout is essential or simultaneous comparison is a primary task.
accessibility_implications: Reflow and info relationship criteria govern contextually; source code inspection is not runtime conformance.
performance_implications: No render or loading performance result established.
responsive_implications: Evaluate placement, content order, discoverability and navigation after each significant composition change.
implementation_notes: No React adoption implied by Primer's reference snapshot.
No universal 8px grid, breakpoint or one-column law.

counterexamples.summary: Full-width high-density content and intrinsically two-dimensional data may need a different responsive strategy.
counterexamples.context: Professional data workbench; WCAG 1.4.10 exception for genuinely 2D content.
